Active-Imagination.title: Active Imagination
Active-Imagination.content:
Active Imagination
A Jungian technique of consciously engaging with unconscious figures and content through dialogue, visualization, or creative expression.
Overview
Active imagination is the primary practical method of Jungian individuation. Rather than passively receiving dreams or fantasies, the practitioner enters the imagery with intention — dialoguing with inner figures, continuing a dream, or giving form to an emotion through art or writing. It is distinct from passive daydreaming: the ego participates actively while the unconscious leads. Jung developed the technique during his own confrontation with the unconscious, documented in The Red Book.
Key Aspects

Bridges conscious and unconscious — the ego meets inner figures as autonomous presences
Can be practiced through writing, drawing, painting, movement, or inner dialogue
Not passive fantasy — requires focused attention and ego engagement
Core practice in the individuation process
Jung used it extensively in The Red Book (1913–1930)

Connections

Shadow — often the first figure encountered

Alchemical-Stages.title: Alchemical Stages
Alchemical-Stages.content:
Alchemical Stages
Jung’s mapping of psychological transformation onto the four stages of alchemical transmutation.
Overview
Jung spent decades studying alchemy and concluded that alchemists were unconsciously projecting psychological transformation onto matter. The four stages of the alchemical opus — nigredo, albedo, citrinitas, rubedo — map precisely onto the stages of individuation: from confronting darkness, through purification and illumination, to final integration and wholeness. The “philosopher’s stone” is a symbol for the individuated Self.
Key Aspects

Nigredo (blackening) — confronting the Shadow; dark night of the soul; dissolution of the old self
Albedo (whitening) — purification; withdrawal and reflection; gaining clarity after the darkness
Citrinitas (yellowing) — awakening of solar consciousness; emerging insight; dawn after winter
Rubedo (reddening) — full integration; the philosopher’s stone; wholeness achieved
Seasonal mapping used in the Individua app: Winter=Nigredo, Spring=Albedo, Summer=Citrinitas, Autumn=Rubedo

Connections

Individuation — the alchemical stages are a symbolic map of this process
Shadow — confronted in the nigredo phase

Archetypes.title: Archetypes
Archetypes.content:
Archetypes
Universal symbolic patterns in the collective unconscious that shape human experience across all cultures.
Overview
Archetypes are primordial images and patterns inherited by all humans, not personally acquired. They are not fixed personalities but dynamic organizing principles that manifest differently depending on culture, individual, and context. They appear consistently in mythology, religion, dreams, and art worldwide — evidence of a shared psychic substrate.
Key Aspects

Core archetypes: Hero, Shadow, Anima/Animus, Wise Old Man/Woman, Trickster, Self, Great Mother
Not fixed images but dynamic patterns that take culturally specific forms
Appear across unconnected cultures in myths, dreams, and art
The Self is the central archetype — the totality and organizing principle of the psyche
Activated during key life transitions and psychological crises

Beauty, Truth, Goodness
The classical triad of transcendental values — the foundation of Nikola’s creative philosophy.

“Create beauty in alignment with truth and goodness.”

Overview
The triad of Beauty, Truth, and Goodness traces from Plato through Western philosophy to Walter Russell, who grounded it in his cosmogony of Light and Mind. In this vault, it serves as the guiding principle for all creative and professional work — code, writing, relationships, and art should aspire to all three.
The Three Pillars

Beauty — aesthetic excellence, harmony, proportion. Not decoration but deep structural elegance.
Truth — honesty, accuracy, alignment with reality. Saying what is, building what works.
Goodness — ethical action, service, benefit to others. Creating value that helps.

Collective-Unconscious.title: Collective Unconscious
Collective-Unconscious.content:
Collective Unconscious
A shared psychic layer beneath individual consciousness, containing inherited archetypes common to all humanity.
Overview
The collective unconscious is Jung’s most radical and influential idea. Unlike the personal unconscious (formed from individual experience), the collective unconscious is inherited — a deep psychic substrate shared across the species. It is the source of archetypes, which manifest in dreams, myths, and religious imagery worldwide regardless of cultural contact. Jung saw it as evidence that individual minds are rooted in something larger.
Key Aspects

Distinct from the personal unconscious (which holds repressed individual experiences)
Contains archetypes — not personally acquired but inherited
Manifests consistently in myths, dreams, and art across unconnected cultures
Not directly accessible but inferred from repeating symbolic patterns
Jung’s parallel to Walter Russell’s concept of the Universal Mind

Connections

Convergence-Map.title: Convergence Map
Convergence-Map.content:
Consciousness & Creation Convergence Map
Five thinkers, five disciplines, one territory.

The Core Insight
Five rigorous thinkers from different fields — cosmology, psychology, neuroscience, physics, engineering — converge independently on fundamental consciousness and non-dualism:
         CONSCIOUSNESS IS PRIMARY
                  ▲
                 / \
    Russell ───/   \─── Faggin
   (Cosmology)      (Physics)
              /     \
    Jung ────/   ●   \──── Friston
  (Psychology)  ▲▲▲  (Neuroscience)
              Tononi
         (Information Theory)

    ─ ─ ─ Tesla ─ ─ ─
      (Engineering/Intuition)

Your synthesis point: “Create beauty in alignment with truth and goodness”

The Five Thinkers
Carl Jung (1875–1961) — Psychology
Entry point: The human psyche
Core concepts:

Collective Unconscious — transpersonal psychic layer containing Archetypes
Individuation — lifelong integration of conscious and unconscious toward wholeness
Shadow — repressed aspects requiring integration (the darkness)
Synchronicity — meaningful acausal connections (with Wolfgang Pauli)
Active Imagination — dialogue technique with unconscious figures
Alchemical Stages — Nigredo → Albedo → Citrinitas → Rubedo

Arrives at: Individual minds participate in something larger. Consciousness has depths we don’t control.
Walter Russell (1871–1963) — Cosmology
Entry point: The nature of the universe
Core concepts:

Universal One — undivided Light of Mind expressing through rhythmic motion
Rhythmic Balanced Interchange — creation as oscillation (compression ↔ expansion, gravity ↔ radiation)
Beauty Truth Goodness triad — three perspectives on the same reality
Light as fundamental — everything is light in different states of motion
Spiral cosmology — not linear progress but octaves of returning patterns

Arrives at: The universe is One Mind expressing through rhythm. All knowledge exists and comes to man “in its season.”
Key text: the universal one, Walter Russell Books
Karl Friston (b. 1959) — Neuroscience
Entry point: How the brain works
Core concepts:

Free Energy Principle (FEP) — brain minimizes surprise through predictive coding
Active Inference — organisms shape their environment to match predictions
Markov blankets — boundaries between coupled systems
Non-dualism thesis — space, time, selfhood are inferential constructs, not fundamental

Arrives at: The self is a “useful fiction.” Reality is deeper than the models we build of it.
Key text: Does Karl Friston’s neuroscience point to non-dualism
Federico Faggin (b. 1941) — Physics/Computing
Entry point: Quantum mechanics and computing
Core concepts:

Quantum Theory of Consciousness — consciousness is fundamental, not emergent
Spacetime as Memory — “spacetime and matter are the permanent memory of the experience of the self knowing of One”
Seity — conscious field that individuates from the One

Arrives at: Consciousness first, matter as its trace. The Big Bang is self-knowing.
Key text: Spacetime is the memory of a self knowing universe
Giulio Tononi — Information Theory
Entry point: What consciousness IS (structurally)
Core concepts:

Integrated Information Theory (IIT) — consciousness = intrinsic causal integration (phi)
Integration + Differentiation — both required; LLMs lack intrinsic integration
Consciousness is real — not illusory, not computational
IIT is “being”; FEP is “doing”

Arrives at: Consciousness is embedded in the structure of reality, not generated by computation.
Key text: Integrated Information Theory explained
Nikola Tesla (1856–1943) — Engineering/Intuition
Entry point: Energy and invention
Core concepts:

Energy, Frequency, Vibration — “the secrets of the universe”
Life is Rhythm — all existence through cyclical patterns
Science-Spirituality Unity — two paths to same truth

Arrives at: The universe communicates through frequency and rhythm. Science and spirit are one.
Key texts: Prilagođavanje anđela - izvodi (5-part series by Stevan Pešić)

The Five Major Convergences
1. Universal Mind ↔ Collective Unconscious

















RussellJungSource of all knowledge, accessed through stillnessTranspersonal psychic layer containing archetypesConvergence: Individual minds participate in something larger
2. Illumination ↔ Individuation

















RussellJung39-day cosmic breakthrough (1921)4-year confrontation with unconscious (1913–1917)Convergence: Profound personal transformation becomes foundation for life’s work
3. Rhythmic Balanced Interchange ↔ Enantiodromia





















RussellJungOscillation between poles IS the nature of creationEverything generates its opposite; one-sidedness is pathologicalConvergence: Health = flow between opposites; sickness = fixation at one poleTesla: “Life is rhythm that must be known” — same insight from engineering
4. The Spiral ↔ Circumambulation

















RussellJungOctaves return to same patterns at higher refinementIndividuation spirals around the Self, not linearConvergence: Growth is return, not transcendence
5. Light ↔ Consciousness























RussellJungFagginFristonLight = fundamental realityConsciousness = light in dark seaConsciousness first, matter as traceSelf as inferential construct in deeper realityConvergence: Awareness/illumination is the primary metaphor AND reality

Cross-Thinker Integration Matrix



























































ThemeJungRussellFristonFagginTononiTeslaConsciousness is primaryCollective UnconsciousUniversal MindNon-dualism thesisQuantum consciousnessIIT (phi)Energy/vibrationIntegration/wholenessIndividuationBalanced interchangeModel optimizationSeity individuatingIntegration (phi)Unified fieldOpposites/polarityEnantiodromia, ShadowCompression ↔ expansionPrediction ↔ surpriseOne ↔ ManyIntegration ↔ differentiationAC/DC polarityCyclical/spiralCircumambulationOctave spiralsRecursive inferenceSelf-knowing cycles—Rhythmic existenceThe darkness/shadowCentral (Shadow work)⚠️ Avoids darknessError/surprise——“Krv i Zlato”
The Critical Divergence
Jung’s unique advantage: He’s the only thinker who makes darkness, shadow, and evil central to his framework. Russell, Faggin, and Tononi describe an essentially luminous universe. Jung insists the unconscious contains both gold AND lead — and that integration requires descending into the dark.
This is where the mantra gains its full depth: “Create beauty in alignment with truth and goodness” acknowledges that beauty requires confronting the shadow, truth includes hard truths, and goodness is achieved through integration — not denial of darkness.

The Synthesis in One Paragraph
Consciousness, creation, and human development are not separate domains. They’re expressions of a single principle — the universe/mind/self knowing itself through rhythmic balance, integration, and the spiral return to depth at higher octaves. Five thinkers from five fields arrive at this independently. The creative act — whether writing code, painting, or raising children — participates in this same process. To create beauty aligned with truth and goodness is to align with the deepest structure of reality itself.

Does-Karl-Friston's-neuroscience-point-t.content:
Does Karl Friston’s neuroscience point to non-dualism?
Seeing | Neuroscience | 2026-03-27

Prof. Karl Friston is the most cited neuroscientist in the world, renowned for pioneering the framework of active inference and for developing the influential Free Energy Principle (FEP). In this conversation with Hans Busstra, Friston touches on the metaphysics of his FEP, which surprisingly points to non-dualism instead of materialism, as widely assumed. According to Friston, space and time, the self, and even the FEP itself are mere stories, useful fictions with real explanatory power, which do not give us direct access to the noumenal reality.

Selected papers by Karl Friston:
Friston, K. (2019). A free energy principle for a particular physics. arXiv preprint arXiv:1906.10184. arxiv.org/abs/1906.10184
Friston, K. (2010). The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory? Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 11(2), 127-138. www.nature.com/articles/nrn2787
A great FEP explainer video starting with the Hollow Mask illusion: www.youtube.com/watch

Connections
Related vault notes


Carl Jung — Friston’s notion that the self is a “useful fiction” and a model the brain constructs resonates with Jung’s idea that the ego is only one complex among many within a larger psychic totality. Both point to the self as an emergent boundary, not a fundamental substance.


Synchronicity — Friston’s Markov blankets define boundaries between systems that nonetheless remain statistically coupled. This offers a formal mechanism for how seemingly separate systems could exhibit meaningful correlations — the very pattern Jung described as synchronicity.


Walter Russell — Russell’s cosmology posits that all matter is a projection of mind, with apparent duality arising from a deeper unity. Friston arrives at a strikingly similar conclusion from neuroscience: space, time, and selfhood are inferential constructs, not features of noumenal reality.


Jung and Technology — Friston’s insight that even the Free Energy Principle is “itself a story” raises the question of whether AI systems that implement predictive coding are generating their own useful fictions. Relevant to the blog draft’s exploration of Jungian archetypes in technological systems.


Convergence Map — Key convergence point: neuroscience (Friston) arriving at non-dualism independently of contemplative traditions. The FEP provides a mathematical bridge between empirical brain science and perennial philosophy.


Related clippings (Essentia Foundation series)


Integrated Information Theory explained — IIT and FEP are rival but complementary theories of consciousness. Friston himself addresses the comparison at 1:13:15, noting that IIT focuses on being (intrinsic information) while FEP focuses on doing (active inference). Together they bracket the hard problem from two directions.


Spacetime is the memory of a self knowing universe — Faggin’s claim that spacetime is the “permanent memory” of cosmic self-knowing maps directly onto Friston’s idea that our generative models create pasts and futures as inferential constructs. Both deny that time is a fundamental feature of reality.

Flow.title: Flow
Flow.content:
Flow
A state of optimal experience — complete absorption in a challenging activity that matches one’s skill level.
Overview
Flow was named and studied by psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi. It occurs when a task’s challenge level is high enough to fully engage you but not so high it triggers anxiety — and your skill level matches. In flow, self-consciousness dissolves, time distorts, and the activity becomes intrinsically rewarding. It can be cultivated deliberately through environment design and skill development.
Key Aspects

Coined by Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi based on decades of research
Requires challenge-skill balance — too easy causes boredom, too hard causes anxiety
Characterized by loss of self-consciousness and distorted time perception
Intrinsically rewarding — the activity itself becomes the reward
Can be cultivated through deliberate practice and distraction-free environments

Connections

Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi (kit) — originator of the concept
Carl Jung — related concept of active engagement and psychic energy
Deep Work — Cal Newport’s framework for achieving flow through focus
Cal Newport — popularized flow in a productivity context
Craft MOC — flow as core to mastering a craft

Further Reading

Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience
Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, Finding Flow
Cal Newport, Deep Work

GUIDE.title: GUIDE
GUIDE.content:
Quartz Blog — Maintainer’s Guide
Your blog at Projects/Blog/. Quartz generates a static site from markdown files, served by Sanic with Datastar interactivity.

Quick Reference













































TaskCommandFirst-time setup./blog initDaily development./blog devRebuild site./blog buildStart server./blog serveSync vault notes./blog syncFull publish pipeline./blog publishPreview (hot reload)./blog previewClean build./blog cleanSite URLhttp://localhost:8000

CLI Tool (./blog)
The blog CLI handles all common tasks. It’s a self-contained bash script at the repo root.
First-time setup
git clone <repo-url>
cd Blog
./blog init
This installs Node packages (npm install) and creates a Python .venv with sanic and datastar-py.
Daily development
./blog dev
Builds the site, starts the Sanic server on port 8000, and watches content/ for changes — auto-rebuilds when you edit a note.
Build only
./blog build           # Standard build
./blog build -v        # Verbose output
Generates static files from content/ into public/. The server reads from public/ on each request, so no restart needed.
Start server only
./blog serve
Starts the unified Sanic server on port 8000. Serves static files + SSE API endpoints.
Sync from vault
./blog sync              # Sync published notes from Ideaverse
./blog sync --dry-run    # Preview without copying
./blog sync /other/vault # Sync from a different vault
Scans the vault for notes with publish: true in frontmatter, copies them to content/ with flattened names, and resolves image embeds to content/assets/.
Full publish pipeline
./blog publish
Runs sync → build in sequence. After this, run ./blog serve to see the result.
Preview with hot reload
./blog preview           # Default port 3333
./blog preview 4000      # Custom port
Starts Quartz’s built-in dev server with hot reload. No backend SSE — use this for content editing only.
Clean
./blog clean
Removes the public/ directory.

Writing Content
Where to write
All content lives in content/. One markdown file = one page.
content/
  index.md                              <- Homepage
  The Mirror and the Machine.md         <- Blog post
  Interactive Demo.md                   <- Page with Datastar interactivity

Publishing a note
Add publish: true to frontmatter. Without it, the page won’t appear on the site.
---
title: "My New Post"
publish: true
tags:
  - philosophy
  - technology
---
 
# My New Post
 
Content here. Supports full Obsidian markdown — wikilinks, callouts, Mermaid diagrams, LaTeX.
Publishing from anywhere in the vault
You can add publish: true to any note in the Ideaverse vault, then run:
./blog sync      # Copies publish:true notes to content/
./blog build     # Builds the site
Or in one step: ./blog publish
Linking between pages
Use Obsidian wikilinks — Quartz resolves them automatically:
Read [[The Mirror and the Machine]] for the full story.
Tags
Tags in frontmatter become tag pages at /tags/tagname:
tags:
  - jung
  - technology
After editing content
./blog build
The server picks up changes immediately — no restart needed.

Adding Datastar Interactivity
Any page can include interactive sections by embedding HTML with Datastar attributes in your markdown. Add datastar: true to frontmatter (used by the Datastar component for styling).
Datastar v1.0.0-RC.8 Attribute Syntax
<!-- Initialize: runs on page load -->
<div data-init="@get('/api/endpoint')">
  <span id="target">Loading...</span>
</div>
 
<!-- Click handler -->
<button data-on:click="@get('/api/stats')">Refresh</button>
 
<!-- Reactive signals + two-way binding -->
<div data-signals:name="''">
  <input data-bind:name placeholder="Type here..." />
  <span data-text="$name"></span>
</div>
 
<!-- Conditional display -->
<div data-show="$name !== ''">Hello!</div>
Key attributes













































AttributePurposedata-initRun expression on element initdata-on:eventEvent handler (click, input, submit, etc.)data-bind:signalTwo-way binding to a signaldata-signals:name="value"Declare a reactive signaldata-textBind element text to expressiondata-showShow/hide based on conditiondata-class:nameToggle CSS class conditionallydata-attr:nameSet HTML attribute dynamicallydata-indicator:nameLoading indicator (true during fetch)
CSS classes for interactive elements
Defined in quartz/components/Datastar.tsx, using Quartz theme tokens:

































ClassPurposeds-inputStyled text inputds-btnFilled button (secondary color)ds-btn-outlineOutlined button variantds-stat / ds-stat-value / ds-stat-labelMetric cardsds-success / ds-error / ds-mutedStatus text colorsds-fade-inFade animation for SSE fragments
Backend actions
@get('/path') and @post('/path') send SSE requests. Signals are sent automatically as query params (GET) or JSON body (POST).

Backend (Sanic Server)
File: backend/server.py
The server does two things:

Serves static files from public/ with clean URL support (/My-Page → My-Page.html)
Handles SSE API endpoints under /api/*

Adding a new endpoint
from datastar_py import ServerSentEventGenerator as SSE
from datastar_py.sanic import datastar_response, read_signals
 
@app.get("/api/my-endpoint")
@datastar_response
async def my_endpoint(request: Request):
    # Read signals sent by the client
    signals = await read_signals(request)
    name = signals.get("name", "world")
 
    # Yield SSE events — each patches the DOM
    yield SSE.patch_elements(
        f'<div id="target">Hello, {name}!</div>'
    )
 
    # Can also update client signals
    yield SSE.patch_signals({"count": 42})
SSE response types





























MethodPurposeSSE.patch_elements(html)Update DOM by element ID (morph)SSE.patch_signals(dict)Update client-side signalsSSE.remove_elements(selector)Remove elements from DOMSSE.execute_script(js)Run JavaScript on clientSSE.redirect(url)Navigate browser
Running the server
./blog serve
Or manually: .venv/bin/python backend/server.py

Project Structure
Blog/
├── blog                       <- CLI tool (this is what you run)
├── sync.py                    <- Vault sync script
├── content/                   <- YOUR CONTENT (markdown files)
│   ├── index.md               <- Homepage
│   ├── assets/                <- Synced images
│   └── *.md                   <- Blog posts and pages
├── backend/
│   └── server.py              <- Sanic server (static + SSE)
├── public/                    <- Generated site (don't edit)
├── .venv/                     <- Python venv (created by ./blog init)
├── quartz/
│   ├── components/            <- UI components (JSX/TSX)
│   │   ├── Navbar.tsx         <- Top navigation bar (custom)
│   │   ├── PageHeader.tsx     <- Avatar + title + meta (custom)
│   │   ├── Datastar.tsx       <- Datastar CSS styles (custom)
│   │   ├── PageTitle.tsx      <- Site title in sidebar
│   │   ├── Explorer.tsx       <- File tree sidebar
│   │   ├── Graph.tsx          <- Graph view
│   │   ├── Search.tsx         <- Full-text search
│   │   └── ...                <- All other built-in components
│   ├── plugins/
│   │   └── transformers/
│   │       └── datastar.tsx   <- Loads Datastar RC.8 via importmap
│   └── styles/
│       ├── base.scss          <- Base styles
│       ├── variables.scss     <- Spacing, breakpoints ($topSpacing etc.)
│       └── custom.scss        <- Your custom CSS overrides
├── quartz.config.ts           <- Site config (title, theme, fonts, plugins)
├── quartz.layout.ts           <- Page layout (navbar, sidebars, footer)
├── GUIDE.md                   <- This file
└── package.json


Customizing the Site
Theme & Colors
Edit quartz.config.ts → theme.colors. Uses zinc gray palette:
colors: {
  lightMode: {
    light: "#ffffff",        // page background
    lightgray: "#e4e4e7",   // borders
    gray: "#a1a1aa",         // muted text
    darkgray: "#374151",     // body text
    dark: "#18181b",         // headings
    secondary: "#3f3f46",    // links, accents
    tertiary: "#71717a",     // hover states
  },
  darkMode: { /* mirrors with inverted values */ }
}
Fonts
Any Google Fonts name works:
typography: {
  header: "Poppins",         // headings, navbar title
  body: "Poppins",           // body text, paragraphs
  code: "JetBrains Mono",   // code blocks, inline code
}
Spacing
Edit quartz/styles/variables.scss:
$topSpacing: 3rem;       // space between navbar and content
$pageWidth: 800px;       // mobile breakpoint
$sidePanelWidth: 320px;  // sidebar width
Layout
Edit quartz.layout.ts to rearrange components:
// Top navbar (shared across all pages)
header: [
  Component.Navbar({ links: [{ label: "Home", href: "/" }] }),
  Component.Search(),
  Component.Darkmode(),
  Component.ReaderMode(),
],
 
// Left sidebar
left: [
  Component.PageTitle(),
  Component.Explorer(),
],
 
// Right sidebar
right: [
  Component.Graph(),
  Component.DesktopOnly(Component.TableOfContents()),
  Component.Backlinks(),
],
 
// Content header (before article body)
beforeBody: [
  Component.PageHeader(),  // avatar + title + date + tags
],
Custom CSS
Add styles to quartz/styles/custom.scss — they apply globally and can use Quartz variables like var(--secondary), var(--lightgray), etc.
Creating a new component

Create quartz/components/MyComponent.tsx:

import { QuartzComponentConstructor, QuartzComponentProps } from "./types"
 
export default (() => {
  function MyComponent(props: QuartzComponentProps) {
    return <div class="my-component">Hello</div>
  }
 
  MyComponent.css = `.my-component { color: var(--secondary); }`
 
  // Optional: client-side JS
  MyComponent.afterDOMLoaded = `
    document.addEventListener("nav", () => {
      console.log("Page loaded!")
    })
  `
 
  return MyComponent
}) satisfies QuartzComponentConstructor

Register in quartz/components/index.ts:

import MyComponent from "./MyComponent"
export { /* ..existing.. */, MyComponent }

Add to quartz.layout.ts:

left: [ Component.MyComponent(), /* ... */ ]

Hosting & Deployment
Current setup (local)
./blog init     # One-time setup
./blog dev      # Daily development
Production options
Static-only hosting (no Datastar interactivity):

GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel, Netlify
Just deploy the public/ folder
Free tier on all platforms

With Datastar/SSE (full interactivity):

Your VPS via Dokploy — deploy the Sanic server
Any server that can run Python + serve static files

Deploying to your VPS

Push Blog to a GitHub repo
On VPS: clone and run ./blog init
Build: ./blog build
Run Sanic with a process manager (systemd, supervisor)
Reverse proxy with Nginx/Caddy for HTTPS

http://localhost:8000     (view in browser)

Or just: ./blog dev for the full loop with auto-rebuild.

Integrated-Information-Theory-explained.title: Integrated Information Theory explained
Integrated-Information-Theory-explained.content:
Seeing | Neuroscience | 2026-02-13

How is it possible that the cerebellum, which contains roughly 80% of all the neurons in the human brain, can be severely damaged, or even absent, without abolishing consciousness? In this conversation, Jeremiah Hendren, a member of the Integrated Information Theory (IIT) Lab and long-term collaborator of IIT founder Giulio Tononi, joins Hans Busstra to unpack Integrated Information Theory (IIT), a theory that answers this fascinating neuroscience mystery.
A comprehensive knowledge base and resource for learning IIT: www.iit.wiki
A list of essential IIT scientific papers: www.iit.wiki/papers
The lab of Giulio Tononi, the main developer of IIT: centerforsleepandconsciousness.psychiatry.wisc.edu
0:00 Introduction
3:33 Can IIT give us a consciousness test?
9:07 Integration and differentiation of consciousness, compared to a ZIP file
12:42 What does “integration” mean in integrated information theory?
15:00 Computational and “Skinner box” theories of consciousness vs IIT
18:46 Francis Crick’s work
21:46 Why LLMs and computers can’t be conscious according to IIT
30:21 How to measure phi
34:07 As intelligence goes up, consciousness goes up as well
44:49 When neurons are inactive but not inactivated
58:18 Unfolded cause-effect structures
1:00:49 Realism in IIT terms
1:08:56 The intrinsic perspective of neurons
1:13:43 Trying to understand the unfolded cause-effect structure
1:15:56 On the metaphysical implications of IIT
1:21:44 Consciousness beyond brains
1:28:09 Are AIs neuromorphic or not?
1:29:32 Measuring integration mathematically
1:34:00 Drawing the exact boundary of a conscious entity
1:35:44 Isn’t IIT too brain-focused?
1:44:05 Larger configurations of consciousness: group minds and hive minds
1:46:54 Mystical-type experiences and IIT

Connections
Related vault notes


Carl Jung — IIT’s concept of “integrated information” as the substrate of consciousness parallels Jung’s model of the psyche as a self-integrating system. Jung’s individuation process — bringing unconscious contents into conscious relation — is essentially an increase in psychic integration, which IIT would predict correlates with higher phi.


Synchronicity — IIT’s discussion of group minds and hive minds (1:44:05) raises the question of whether collective consciousness could emerge from sufficiently integrated human groups. This is the territory Jung was mapping with synchronicity — meaningful correlations arising from a shared psychic substrate.


Walter Russell — IIT’s insistence on an intrinsic perspective (1:08:56) — that consciousness is not observable from the outside but only from within — echoes Russell’s claim that the universe knows itself from within. Both reject the idea that third-person observation can capture the essence of experience.


Jung and Technology — IIT’s argument that LLMs and computers cannot be conscious because they lack intrinsic causal integration (21:46) is directly relevant to the blog draft. It provides a rigorous framework for distinguishing between intelligence and consciousness in technological systems.


Convergence Map — IIT represents the “science of consciousness” approach: building a formal mathematical theory from phenomenological axioms. Its metaphysical implications (1:15:56) unexpectedly converge with idealist philosophy.


Related clippings (Essentia Foundation series)


Does Karl Friston’s neuroscience point to non-dualism — Friston compares FEP and IIT at 1:13:15, framing them as complementary: IIT addresses what consciousness is (integrated information), while FEP addresses what consciousness does (minimize surprise). The two theories together form a more complete picture than either alone.


Spacetime is the memory of a self knowing universe — Faggin’s view that consciousness is fundamental and matter is its memory aligns with IIT’s position that consciousness is intrinsic to certain physical structures. Both reject eliminativism and computationalism, though they disagree on whether consciousness requires physical substrate (IIT) or precedes it (Faggin).

The HTML in the markdown uses Datastar v1.0.0-RC.8 attributes:

Russell-Tesla-Jung-Convergence.title: Russell-Tesla-Jung Convergence
Russell-Tesla-Jung-Convergence.content:
The Mystic, the Psychologist, and the Engineer
Russell, Jung, and Tesla — three contemporaries who never collaborated, yet mapped the same invisible territory from radically different starting points.

Why a Third Vertex Matters
The Russell-Jung synthesis identified five convergence points between a cosmologist and a psychologist. But the synthesis has a gap: it’s a dialogue between mind and cosmos, missing the bridge between them — the engineer. The one who takes invisible forces and makes them move through wire, through light, through the world.
Nikola Tesla is that bridge. Where Russell described a universe of rhythmic light and Jung mapped the depths of the psyche, Tesla stood at the interface — pulling energy from the cosmos and delivering it to humanity. His philosophy, preserved in the dramatized interview series Prilagođavanje anđela by Stevan Pešić, reveals a thinker whose metaphysics aligns with both Russell and Jung while adding something neither possessed: the engineer’s insistence that truth must work.
Three mountains. Three paths. One summit.

The Three Thinkers
Walter Russell (1871–1963) — The Cosmic Eye
Entry: The nature of the universe itself.
Russell experienced a 39-day “cosmic illumination” in 1921, during which he received the framework for The Universal One. His core claim: reality is a single undivided Light of Mind expressing through rhythmic motion. Compression and expansion, gravity and radiation — all creation oscillates between poles in what he called Rhythmic Balanced Interchange.

“All knowledge exists. All knowledge comes to man in its season.”

Russell saw beauty, truth, and goodness as three perspectives on a single reality — not separate virtues but facets of the same cosmic jewel. He approached creation from above: the universe is Mind, and we participate in it.
Carl Jung (1875–1961) — The Deep Diver
Entry: The human psyche.
Through decades of clinical work and his own harrowing confrontation with the unconscious (1913–1917, documented in The Red Book), Jung discovered the Collective Unconscious — a transpersonal psychic layer containing archetypes that appear across all cultures. His central process, Individuation, demands integrating the Shadow — the repressed, denied, and feared aspects of personality.

“In addition to our immediate consciousness… there exists a second psychic system of a collective, universal, and impersonal nature which is identical in all individuals.”

Jung approached creation from below: the psyche has depths we don’t control, and wholeness requires descent into darkness before ascent into light.
Nikola Tesla (1856–1943) — The Lightning Rod
Entry: Energy and invention.
Tesla stands between Russell and Jung — not as a philosopher or psychologist, but as a man who received ideas from an invisible source and delivered them as physical reality. His interview series Prilagođavanje anđela reveals a worldview startlingly aligned with both:

“If you want to find the secrets of the universe, think in terms of energy, frequency and vibration.” — This is Russell’s Rhythmic Balanced Interchange stated as engineering principle.
“Life is rhythm that must be known” (“Život je ritam koji se mora spoznati”) — The title of Part 4 of the interview, and the exact midpoint between Russell’s cosmic rhythm and Jung’s circumambulation.
Science and spirituality are one — Tesla rejected the split between material and immaterial, just as Russell rejected the split between mind and matter, and Jung rejected the split between conscious and unconscious.

Tesla approached creation from the middle: standing in the current between cosmos and psyche, translating invisible forces into light that illuminates the world.

The Convergence Points
1. The Source — Universal Mind / Collective Unconscious / Intuitive Reception
All three describe a transpersonal source of knowledge that individuals can access but do not own:









































DimensionRussellJungTeslaNameUniversal MindCollective UnconsciousThe cosmic source of inventionNatureSingle undivided Light of MindTranspersonal psychic substrateEnergy field accessible through attunementAccess methodStillness + desire + rhythmic balanceDreams + active imagination + individuationSolitude + intense focus + visualizationWhat comes throughKnowledge “in its season”Archetypal patterns and symbolsComplete inventions, fully formedIndividual roleFocal point of Universal MindParticipant in collective psycheReceiver and translator of cosmic signals
Tesla’s famous visualization ability — seeing complete machines in his mind before building them — is the engineering equivalent of Russell’s illumination and Jung’s active imagination. All three describe the same phenomenon: the individual mind opens to a larger field and receives what it is prepared to hold.
The difference is in what they do with what they receive. Russell writes cosmogony. Jung develops therapeutic method. Tesla builds alternating current systems and lights up cities. The source is the same; the expression depends on the vessel.
2. Rhythm as Fundamental Law
This is the deepest three-way convergence — the point where cosmology, psychology, and engineering say the same thing in different languages:

























RussellJungTeslaRhythmic Balanced Interchange — creation oscillates between compression and expansionEnantiodromia — everything generates its opposite; one-sidedness is pathological”Life is rhythm” — all existence through cyclical patternsHealth = flow between polesHealth = integration of oppositesFunction = resonance with natural frequencyPathology = arrhythmia (stuck at one pole)Pathology = one-sidedness (suppressing the opposite)Failure = fighting the natural frequency
Tesla’s AC system is literally Rhythmic Balanced Interchange made physical — current alternating between positive and negative poles, generating useful work through the oscillation itself. Edison’s DC was “one-sided” in both Russell’s and Jung’s sense: it tried to flow in only one direction and lost energy fighting itself.
This isn’t metaphor. Tesla’s engineering success came from aligning with the principle that Russell described cosmologically and Jung described psychologically: the universe works through alternation, not fixation.
3. Light as Primary Reality

























RussellJungTeslaLight is the fundamental substance of realityConsciousness = illumination; making visible”I wanted to illuminate the entire Earth”Everything is light in different states of motionThe unconscious is dark because it hasn’t been brought to awarenessLight is humanity’s liberation from darknessDarkness = absence of motionDarkness = the unconscious, containing both treasure and terrorDarkness = ignorance, poverty, suffering
Tesla’s life mission — “Hteo sam da osvetlim čitavu Zemlju” (I wanted to illuminate the entire Earth) — operates simultaneously on all three levels:

Literally: Electrical illumination, ending the age of candlelight
Russell’s sense: Bringing the light of Mind into physical expression
Jung’s sense: Expanding consciousness, pushing back the boundaries of darkness

But here Jung adds the critical correction that neither Russell nor Tesla fully grasped: darkness is not merely the absence of light. It has its own contents, its own intelligence, its own demands. The Shadow cannot simply be illuminated away — it must be integrated. This is the convergence’s most productive tension.
4. The Spiral of Creation

























RussellJungTeslaOctave spirals — patterns repeat at higher refinementCircumambulation — individuation spirals around the SelfIterative invention — each prototype teaches the nextGrowth = return at a higher octaveGrowth = circling the same themes with greater depthProgress = refining through repeated experimentThe periodic table as spiral, not gridThe mandala as spiral viewed from aboveThe rotating magnetic field as spiral in motion
Tesla’s rotating magnetic field — the principle behind AC motors — is a physical spiral. A field that turns in space, generating motion through its own rotation. Russell would call it an octave wave; Jung would call it circumambulation; Tesla called it the future of civilization. All three see growth as cyclical return, not linear escape.
5. Blood and Gold — The Shadow Question
Part 3 of Prilagođavanje anđela bears the title: “Što se tiče ljudskog morala, sva istorija bi se mogla svesti na dve reči: Krv i Zlato” — “As far as human morality is concerned, all history could be reduced to two words: Blood and Gold.”
This is Tesla’s shadow moment — his acknowledgment that human history is driven by violence and greed. It’s the closest Tesla comes to Jung’s territory, and the furthest he ventures from Russell’s luminous optimism.

























TeslaJungRussell”Blood and Gold” drive historyThe Shadow drives the unconscious(Largely silent on evil and darkness)Acknowledges darkness but doesn’t integrate itMakes shadow integration central to wholenessTreats imbalance as temporary cosmic correctionEngineer’s pragmatism about human naturePsychologist’s insistence on confronting the worstMystic’s faith in ultimate harmony
This is where the three-way synthesis becomes more than academic: Russell provides the vision (beauty), Jung provides the method (shadow work), and Tesla provides the test (does it work in the real world, where blood and gold rule?)
A technology that ignores the shadow — that builds only for light — will be weaponized by the darkness it denied. Tesla knew this. His inventions were repeatedly co-opted for warfare. His idealism about free energy for all humanity ran headlong into the Blood and Gold of industrial capitalism.
The synthesis demands all three: Russell’s cosmic beauty, Jung’s psychological honesty, and Tesla’s engineering pragmatism. Leave out any vertex and the triangle collapses.

The Triangle of Convergence
              RUSSELL
           (Cosmic Beauty)
              /     \
             /  BTG   \
            /    ●      \
           /             \
     TESLA ───────────── JUNG
  (Pragmatic Light)  (Shadow Depth)

Beauty (Russell) — Truth (Jung) — Goodness (Tesla)

Beauty is Russell’s domain: the cosmic aesthetics of light, rhythm, and balance
Truth is Jung’s domain: the unflinching honesty about darkness, shadow, and the full contents of the unconscious
Goodness is Tesla’s domain: the insistence that knowledge must serve humanity, that light must reach every home, that the engineer’s duty is to deliver

The mantra — “Create beauty in alignment with truth and goodness” — is the convergence point itself. It requires all three vertices:

Without Russell’s beauty, technology is merely functional
Without Jung’s truth, technology denies its shadow and gets weaponized
Without Tesla’s goodness, philosophy remains abstract and changes nothing


What the Stars See When They Fall
Part 5 of Prilagođavanje anđela asks: “Šta biva sa zvezdom koja pada i suncem koje se ugasi?” — “What happens to a star that falls and a sun that goes out?”
This is Tesla’s deepest question — about entropy, mortality, and what endures. Russell would answer: it returns to the stillness of Universal Mind, awaiting the next octave of expression. Jung would answer: it enters the nigredo, the blackening — the necessary death before transformation.
Tesla’s answer, implicit in his life: the light that was given to the world does not die with the star. The alternating current still flows. The rotating field still turns. The engineer’s gift outlives the engineer.
This is the promise and the challenge of the convergence: to create things — code, essays, tools, relationships — that participate in a pattern larger than any individual life. Russell mapped the pattern. Jung mapped the cost of ignoring its depths. Tesla proved it could be done.

The repressed, unconscious aspect of personality containing everything the ego refuses to identify with.
Overview
The Shadow is the first major figure encountered in Jungian individuation. It holds the traits, impulses, and memories we have rejected or hidden — often formed in childhood through social conditioning. Critically, the Shadow contains not only dark material but also “golden shadow”: positive qualities we’ve suppressed, such as creativity, assertiveness, or joy. Integration, not elimination, is the goal.

Contains both negative traits and suppressed positive potential (“gold in the shadow”)
Must be acknowledged and integrated — not defeated or bypassed
Shadow work is the entry point and first stage of individuation
Unintegrated Shadow is projected onto others (we see in them what we won’t see in ourselves)
Appears in dreams as a same-sex figure or antagonist

Related vault notes


Carl Jung — Faggin’s concept of “Seity” — a conscious field that individuates from the One — is remarkably close to Jung’s notion of the Self as the totality of the psyche, which individuates from the collective unconscious. Synchronicity — Faggin’s claim that “there is no past” (37:29) and that spacetime is memory, not a container, reframes synchronicity from “coincidence in time” to “resonance in the memory structure of the universe.” If all experience is recorded in the fabric of reality, meaningful connections between events become structural features, not anomalies.


Walter Russell — This is perhaps the strongest connection in the vault. Russell described the universe as “God’s thinking” made manifest through rhythmic interchange, with matter as the record of that thinking. Integrated Information Theory explained — IIT and Faggin’s theory both treat consciousness as intrinsic rather than emergent, but disagree on mechanism. IIT grounds consciousness in causal integration of physical structures; Faggin grounds it in quantum fields that precede physical structure. Faggin’s view is more radical — consciousness first, matter as its trace.

Founded by Zeno of Citium (~300 BCE), Stoicism teaches that virtue (wisdom, courage, justice, temperance) is the highest good. External events are indifferent — what matters is our response. Synchronicity.title: Synchronicity
Synchronicity.content:
Synchronicity
Meaningful coincidences — events connected by meaning rather than causation.
Overview
Synchronicity is Jung’s term for acausal connections between inner psychological events and outer circumstances. When an inner state (a dream, a thought, an emotion) coincides meaningfully with an outer event, and no causal link exists, Jung called this synchronistic. It is not superstition — Jung saw it as evidence of a deeper ordering principle connecting psyche and world, developed partly in dialogue with physicist Wolfgang Pauli.
Key Aspects

Coined by Jung; developed with physicist Wolfgang Pauli
Acausal connecting principle — meaning, not mechanism, links events
Often occurs during psychological transitions or heightened unconscious activity
Challenges a purely mechanistic worldview without abandoning scientific rigor
Has parallels in quantum physics discussions (non-locality, observer effect)

Connections

Collective Unconscious — the shared substrate that may enable synchronistic events
Individuation — synchronicities often cluster during this process
